quotes.text: AI does not remove bottlenecks by itself. It exposes them. Once exposed, those bottlenecks are often leadership shaped.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes AI as a diagnostic that reveals leadership-shaped bottlenecks rather than a fix for them.

quotes.text: When decision quality depends on one leader touching too many things, the organization is not well controlled. It is fragile.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concisely states why heavy personal control creates fragility instead of safety.

quotes.text: a dashboard increases visibility but it does not automatically increase decision readiness. And those are not the same thing.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Separates visibility from the ability to act, a common misconception in AI-era reporting.

quotes.text: Power platform sprawl is rarely just a governance problem. It is a signal. It shows you exactly where your official operating model is too slow, too rigid or too disconnected from business reality.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Turns citizen-development sprawl into a diagnostic signal instead of a reason to lock down.

quotes.text: Ownership without access isn't empowerment. It is just structural theatre that sets people up for failure.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A sharp rule for aligning responsibility with the access needed to act.

takeaways: AI lowers the cost of analysis, so leadership control that once reduced risk now turns into latency and a single point of failure.
Leaders should replace personal approvals with explicit context, decision classes, escalation thresholds and aligned decision, data and intervention rights.
Measure decision latency, dependency rate, ownership clarity, override patterns and rework instead of activity or license usage.
hook: Many leaders respond to AI with more approvals and oversight, and then wonder why Copilot and Power Platform deliver so little value. This episode shows executives and Microsoft 365 owners why control stops scaling and how to redesign decision systems, rights and feedback loops so teams can act inside clear guardrails.
